functions.name: hashcat_init
functions.signature: int hashcat_init (hashcat_ctx_t *hashcat_ctx, void (*event) (const u32, struct hashcat_ctx *, const void *, const size_t));
functions.description: Initializes a hashcat context and registers an optional event callback. Intended to be called once before any session-related API. The event callback, if non-NULL, must match the provided signature and may be invoked by the library to report events.
requirements: hashcat_ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to a hashcat_ctx_t structure (inferred from signature).
The event callback pointer, if provided, must have the exact signature: void (const u32, struct hashcat_ctx *, const void *, const size_t) (explicit from signature).
Call this function before any hashcat_session_* or query functions (lifecycle inference).
Thread-safety or reentrancy guarantees are unknown.
Return value semantics (success/error) are unknown.

functions.name: hashcat_destroy
functions.description: Releases resources associated with a previously initialized hashcat context. Use after all session activity has ended.
requirements: hashcat_ctx must be a valid pointer previously passed to and initialized by hashcat_init (lifecycle inference).
Must not be called concurrently with other API calls using the same context (state/lifecycle inference).
After this call, the context must not be used again unless reinitialized.
Error reporting is not applicable (void).

functions.name: hashcat_session_init
functions.signature: int hashcat_session_init (hashcat_ctx_t *hashcat_ctx, const char *install_folder, const char *shared_folder, int argc, char **argv, const int comptime);
functions.description: Initializes a cracking session on an existing hashcat context using application/environment parameters. Typically called once per session before execute.
requirements: hashcat_ctx must have been successfully initialized by hashcat_init (lifecycle inference).
install_folder and shared_folder, if non-NULL, must point to NUL-terminated strings (C string convention).
argv must reference at least argc valid NUL-terminated strings (standard argc/argv convention).
comptime is an integer parameter; specific valid range/meaning is unknown.
Return code semantics (0/negative/etc.) are unknown.

functions.name: hashcat_session_execute
functions.description: Runs the prepared session (start cracking/processing) on the given context. Call after successful hashcat_session_init.
requirements: hashcat_ctx must be a valid, initialized session (created via hashcat_init and hashcat_session_init) (lifecycle inference).
May block until completion; exact execution semantics are unknown.
Return code semantics are unknown.

functions.name: hashcat_session_pause
functions.description: Requests the active session to pause. Useful for temporarily halting execution.
requirements: hashcat_ctx must refer to a context with a session that has been started (i.e., after hashcat_session_execute) (lifecycle inference).
Behavior if called when not running is unspecified.
Return code semantics are unknown.

functions.name: hashcat_session_resume
functions.description: Requests a previously paused session to resume.
requirements: hashcat_ctx must refer to a context with a paused session (lifecycle inference).
Behavior if called when not paused is unspecified.
Return code semantics are unknown.

functions.name: hashcat_session_bypass
functions.description: Requests the active session to bypass current work unit(s). Exact behavior depends on internal scheduler.
requirements: hashcat_ctx must refer to a context with an initialized session (lifecycle inference).
Return code semantics are unknown.

functions.name: hashcat_session_checkpoint
functions.description: Triggers a checkpoint save for the active session, allowing later restoration. Often used for long-running tasks.
requirements: hashcat_ctx must refer to a context with an initialized session (lifecycle inference).
Return code semantics are unknown.

functions.name: hashcat_session_finish
functions.description: Signals the session to finish gracefully, performing any necessary shutdown steps.
requirements: hashcat_ctx must refer to a context with an initialized or running session (lifecycle inference).
Return code semantics are unknown.

functions.name: hashcat_session_quit
functions.description: Requests the session to quit. Compared to finish, this may be a more immediate or forceful termination; exact semantics are unspecified.
requirements: hashcat_ctx must refer to a context with an initialized session (lifecycle inference).
Return code semantics are unknown.

functions.name: hashcat_session_destroy
functions.description: Destroys and cleans up the current session associated with the context. Call after a session is finished/quit and before hashcat_destroy.
requirements: hashcat_ctx must refer to a context whose session was previously initialized (hashcat_session_init) (lifecycle inference).
Should be called when no other session API is active on the same context (lifecycle inference).
Return code semantics are unknown.

functions.name: hashcat_get_log
functions.description: Returns a pointer to an internal log buffer or log string for the given context. Use for retrieving recent or accumulated logs.
requirements: hashcat_ctx must be a valid, initialized context (lifecycle inference).
Returned pointer ownership and lifetime are unspecified; treat as read-only and do not free (inference based on common patterns).
The returned pointer may be NULL if no log is available; exact behavior is unknown.

functions.name: hashcat_get_status
functions.description: Retrieves the current status snapshot into the provided hashcat_status_t structure.
requirements: hashcat_ctx must be a valid, initialized context (lifecycle inference).
hashcat_status must be a valid, writable pointer to a hashcat_status_t that the function can populate (inferred from output parameter).
Call may be made during or after session execution; exact timing guarantees are unknown.
Return code semantics are unknown.

generators.generator:
import os
import random
import struct
import string

# Target expects generic C strings used as install/shared folder paths and argv items.
# We generate multiple NUL-terminated strings in one buffer; the harness will slice
# from the buffer per FUZZ_PARAM_STR call. We include a variety of plausible values
# to exercise code paths (empty, relative, absolute, with spaces, options, unicode-ish,
# and typical hashcat-like args like -m, -a, wordlist, mask, hash string).

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_choice(rng, seq):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]

def _rand_ascii(rng, min_len, max_len):
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Avoid embedded NULs; only printable and common punctuations
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_./:+@#%()[]{}=,\t "
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))

def _path_variants(rng):
    # Mix of empty, relative, absolute unix/win-like, with spaces and dots
    drive = chr(rng.randint(67, 90))  # C..Z
    parts = [
        "",
        ".",
        "..",
        "~",
        "/tmp",
        "/var/tmp",
        f"/opt/{_rand_ascii(rng,3,8)}",
        f"/usr/local/share/{_rand_ascii(rng,3,8)}",
        f"C:\\Users\\test\\{_rand_ascii(rng,3,8)}",
        f"{drive}:\\Program Files\\{_rand_ascii(rng,4,10)}",
        f"./build/{_rand_ascii(rng,3,8)}",
        f"../share/{_rand_ascii(rng,3,8)}",
        f"/path/with space/{_rand_ascii(rng,3,6)}",
    ]
    return parts

def _hashcat_arg_variants(rng):
    # Common CLI-like arguments
    masks = [
        "?l?l?l?l?d?d",
        "?u?l?d?s",
        "?a?a?a?a",
        "?1?1?1?1",  # with custom charsets
    ]
    wordlists = [
        "/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt",
        "/tmp/dict.txt",
        "dicts/top1k.txt",
    ]
    hashes = [
        # Some simple representative hashes or identifiers
        "$1$abcdef12$KIXQ7iYfO0n0C2..xyz12/",   # md5crypt-like
        "5d41402abc4b2a76b9719d911017c592",     # md5("hello")
        "sha1:2aae6c35c94fcfb415dbe95f408b9ce91ee846ed",
        "NT:8846f7eaee8fb117ad06bdd830b7586c",
    ]
    modes = ["-m 0", "-m 1000", "-m 22000", "--hash-info", "--benchmark"]
    attacks = ["-a 0", "-a 3", "-a 1"]
    misc = ["--quiet", "--force", "--status-json", "--optimized-kernel-enable", "--potfile-disable"]
    charsets = ["-1 ?l?d", "-2 abc123", "--hex-charset"]

    # Build several argv strings typical of different scenarios
    argv_sets = []
    # Straight attack file mode
    argv_sets.append([_prog_name(rng), _rand_choice(rng, modes), _rand_choice(rng, attacks)])
    argv_sets.append([_prog_name(rng), "-m", str(_rand_mode(rng)), "-a", "0", _rand_choice(rng, wordlists)])
    # Mask attack
    argv_sets.append([_prog_name(rng), "-a", "3", _rand_choice(rng, masks)])
    argv_sets.append([_prog_name(rng), _rand_choice(rng, charsets), "-a", "3", _rand_choice(rng, masks)])
    # Direct hash string
    argv_sets.append([_prog_name(rng), "-m", str(_rand_mode(rng)), _rand_choice(rng, hashes)])
    # Minimal program name only
    argv_sets.append([_prog_name(rng)])
    # Flags only
    argv_sets.append([_prog_name(rng), _rand_choice(rng, misc)])
    # Empty args permitted by harness (argc can be 0); we still provide strings to consume
    argv_sets.append([_prog_name(rng), "", _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 8)])

    # Flatten and deduplicate preserving order
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for av in argv_sets:
        for s in av:
            if s not in seen:
                out.append(s)
                seen.add(s)
    return out

def _prog_name(rng):
    names = ["hashcat", "hc", "hc.bin", "hashcat64", "hashcat.exe"]
    return _rand_choice(rng, names)

def _rand_mode(rng):
    # pick common modes plus some random range
    common = [0, 1000, 1400, 22000, 16800, 3200, 2500]
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return _rand_choice(rng, common)
    return rng.randint(0, 64000)

def _utf8_spice(rng, s):
    # Occasionally insert some UTF-8 multibyte sequences to stress path handling
    if not s:
        return s
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return s
    accents = ["é", "ä", "漢", "字", "✓", "ß", "ø"]
    pos = rng.randint(0, len(s))
    return s[:pos] + _rand_choice(rng, accents) + s[pos:]

def _make_c_string(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Ensure no embedded NUL, then append NUL
    bs = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    bs = bs.split(b"\x00")[0]
    return bs + b"\x00"

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    chunks = []

    # Install/shared folder candidates
    paths = _path_variants(rng)
    rng.shuffle(paths)
    for p in paths[:rng.randint(4, min(10, len(paths)))]:
        chunks.append(_make_c_string(_utf8_spice(rng, p)))

    # Arg strings covering various use-cases
    arg_strings = _hashcat_arg_variants(rng)
    rng.shuffle(arg_strings)
    for a in arg_strings[:rng.randint(6, min(16, len(arg_strings)))]:
        chunks.append(_make_c_string(_utf8_spice(rng, a)))

    # Add a few purely random ascii strings to diversify
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        chunks.append(_make_c_string(_rand_ascii(rng, 0, 20)))

    # Ensure at least one empty string and one single char
    chunks.append(_make_c_string(""))
    chunks.append(_make_c_string("-"))

    buf = b"".join(chunks)
    if len(buf) > MAX_TOTAL:
        buf = buf[:MAX_TOTAL]
        # ensure buffer ends at a NUL to not split a string mid-sequence
        if buf[-1] != 0:
            # find last NUL; if none, replace last byte with NUL
            last_nul = buf.rfind(b"\x00")
            if last_nul == -1:
                buf = buf[:-1] + b"\x00"
            else:
                buf = buf[:last_nul+1]
    return buf

import random
import string
from typing import List

# We generate a single bytes buffer that the harness will slice to fulfill FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# and other requests. Our goal: produce a small set of interesting argv-like strings and
# plausible folder paths to drive hashcat_session_init through different code paths while
# remaining valid.
#
# Encoding format (simple length-prefixed sequence of UTF-8 strings):
#   [u16 count][ repeated: u16 len, bytes payload ]
# The fuzzer stub will request multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() values; typical integration layers
# read sequential strings from the provided buffer. We therefore pack several meaningful
# tokens:
# - install_folder path
# - shared_folder path
# - arg0 (program name)
# - up to a few argument tokens including:
#   * algorithm mode flag and value (-m 0, -m 1000, -m 22000, etc.)
#   * attack mode (-a 0/1/3)
#   * sample hash string (for -m 0 raw MD5) or filename-like token
#   * wordlist filename-like token
#   * mask token (e.g., ?l?d?d)
#   * options like --quiet, --force, --status
# All strings are NUL-terminated by consumer when converted to C strings; we provide raw bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

COMMON_FLAGS = [
    "-m", "-a", "-w", "-O", "--quiet", "--status", "--status-json",
    "--optimized-kernel-enable", "--potfile-disable", "--restore-disable",
]

HASH_MODES = ["0", "100", "500", "900", "1000", "1400", "22000", "3200", "5600"]
ATTACK_MODES = ["0", "1", "3", "6", "7"]

# Some valid-looking hashes for popular modes (kept short and representative)
SAMPLE_HASHES = [
    # MD5 (mode 0)
    "8743b52063cd84097a65d1633f5c74f5",
    # NTLM (1000)
    "32ed87bdb5fdc5e9cba88547376818d4",
    # SHA1 (100)
    "2fd4e1c67a2d28fced849ee1bb76e7391b93eb12",
]

MASKS = ["?d?d?d?d?d?d?d?d", "?l?l?l?l?d?d", "?u?l?l?d?d!", "?a?a?a?a"]

WORDLIST_NAMES = [
    "wordlist.txt", "rockyou.txt", "dict.lst", "wl.gz", "small.txt"
]

PROGRAM_NAMES = [
    "hashcat", "hc", "/usr/bin/hashcat", "C:/Program Files/hashcat/hashcat.exe"
]

FOLDER_PATHS = [
    ".", "./", "/usr/local/share/hashcat", "/tmp/hcshare", "C:/hashcat",
]

EXTRA_TOGGLES = ["--force", "--username", "--hex-charset", "--hex-salt"]


def _rand_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = rng.choice(FOLDER_PATHS)
    # Occasionally add a subdir
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        sub = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-") for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)))
        sep = '/' if '/' in base else ('\\' if ':' in base else '/')
        return f"{base}{sep}{sub}"
    return base


def _argv_set(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    args: List[str] = []

    # Program name
    args.append(rng.choice(PROGRAM_NAMES))

    # Choose a mode/attack pairing
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        args += ["-m", rng.choice(HASH_MODES)]
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        args += ["-a", rng.choice(ATTACK_MODES)]

    # Workload or optimized kernel toggle sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        args += ["-w", str(rng.randint(1, 4))]
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        args.append("-O")

    # Additional toggles
    for flag in rng.sample(EXTRA_TOGGLES, rng.randint(0, min(2, len(EXTRA_TOGGLES)))):
        args.append(flag)

    # Supply target inputs depending on attack mode
    attack = None
    try:
        ai = args.index("-a")
        attack = args[ai + 1]
    except Exception:
        attack = None

    # Provide either hash string directly or a filename-like token
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        args.append(rng.choice(SAMPLE_HASHES))
    else:
        # filename-looking hash source
        name = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 10)))
        ext = rng.choice([".hash", ".txt", ".lst"]) 
        args.append(name + ext)

    # Add wordlist or mask based on attack mode
    if attack == "0" or attack is None:
        # straight attack: add a wordlist path
        wl = rng.choice(WORDLIST_NAMES)
        # Occasionally prepend a folder
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            wl = _rand_path(rng).rstrip("/\\") + ("/" if rng.random() < 0.7 else "\\") + wl
        args.append(wl)
    elif attack == "3":
        args.append(rng.choice(MASKS))
    else:
        # combinator/hybrid: include two wordlists or a wordlist + mask
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            args.append(rng.choice(WORDLIST_NAMES))
            args.append(rng.choice(WORDLIST_NAMES))
        else:
            args.append(rng.choice(WORDLIST_NAMES))
            args.append(rng.choice(MASKS))

    # Keep small (stub caps at max_args=3, but FUZZ harness will sample individual strings)
    return args


def _pack_strings(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # length-prefixed u16 count, then u16 length + payload per string
    out = bytearray()
    def put_u16(x: int):
        out.append((x >> 8) & 0xFF)
        out.append(x & 0xFF)
    # Ensure total does not exceed MAX_TOTAL
    encoded = [s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore') for s in strings]
    # Trim overly long entries
    trimmed = [b[:512] for b in encoded]
    # Build
    put_u16(len(trimmed))
    for b in trimmed:
        put_u16(len(b))
        out += b
    return bytes(out[:MAX_TOTAL])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # install_folder and shared_folder first (FUZZ_PARAM_STR will consume in order)
    install_folder = _rand_path(rng)
    shared_folder = _rand_path(rng)

    argv_list = _argv_set(rng)

    # Add a few extra generic strings to satisfy any additional FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    extras = [
        "--status-timer=10",
        "--outfile-check-timer=5",
        "--session=fuze",
    ]

    strings = [install_folder, shared_folder] + argv_list + extras

    return _pack_strings(strings)
